courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Modern Europe, politics & social change
alternatives.concept: Study modern European history, political institutions, international relations, migration, civil society, identity, conflict, public debate and cultural expression as a related social-science and humanities route. Use France and the Francophone world as evidenced motivating cases while preserving the absence of French-language proficiency and a cumulative France-specific curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: The label describes the completed curriculum’s modern European history, politics, sociology, conflict, media and public-culture content without presenting it as French Language and Culture or French-language training.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and ten level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term and none has a formal prerequisite. Introductory history, politics and sociology precede advanced EU politics, archival research, conflict, social theory, persuasion, literary-film and media analysis. No French-language prerequisite or proficiency is implied.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & cultural identity
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic and media forms create cultural meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal production. Preserve French-language acquisition, French linguistics and France- and Francophone-specific depth as explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film, media and cultural identity; it does not claim French proficiency or a French/Francophone disciplinary curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics by four semesters. Introductory literature, rhetoric, sociology and film/media precede advanced persuasive, creative, interpretive and documentary work. No French-language competence is implied.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses / 75 EC differ in each direction. Comparative politics, international relations, modern sociology, EU politics, historical research, peace and conflict, Western military history, misinformation and environmental movements are replaced by literary studies, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, media archaeology, life writing and community communication. The change shifts the programme from modern European institutions and social change to language, literature and mediated cultural identity.

candidates.label: French proficiency, French linguistics and French-language writing

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. The first develops a modern-European historical, political and social route motivated by France and the Francophone world; the second develops literature, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and mediated cultural expression. A third French-proficiency, French-linguistics and French-language-writing route is not feasible because the current UCR workbook contains no French-language course, cumulative proficiency sequence, French grammar, French sociolinguistics, translation or French-language academic writing. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as French proficiency.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study modern European history and politics, migration, civil society, literature, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and cultural identity. UCR does not offer French proficiency progression, French linguistics, French-language academic work, a cumulative France/Francophone cultural sequence or the required semester abroad, so these are related humanities and social-science routes rather than French Language and Culture equivalents.
